title: Compatibility boundary and Migration Assistant guidelines for runtime
creator: Avery Chen
description: Purpose: Define clear compatibility boundaries for the serving runtime and deliver an automated Migration Assistant (CLI + backend) that helps customers move across minor and major runtime releases with minimal service disruption. Problem: Customers are uncertain which changes are safe to adopt, how to migrate pinned model versions, and how to validate behavior across runtime variants. This ticket captures the policy, the set of signals we will surface, and the concrete migration-assistant behaviors (dry-run, compatibility report, automatic adapters). Scope: policy for compatibility classification, headers and response codes for deprecations, migration-assistant implementation blueprint, telemetry signals for rollout gates, and documentation templates. Non-goals: reworking SDK behavior, changing public REST schema without follow-up deprecation steps (those will be separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A compatibility classification matrix is approved by Release Engineering and Runtime PM. 2) Migration Assistant prototype (CLI + server) that produces a per-customer compatibility report for a target runtime version exists. 3) Report includes API contract diffs, KV-cache behavior fingerprints, and latency/regression risk score. 4) Automated compatibility headers are emitted by the runtime for deprecated endpoints. 5) Canary rollout gating rules consume telemetry and can block/allow auto-upgrade. 6) Docs and customer-facing migration checklist published to the console docs site.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Policy + signals (2 sprints) - Draft compatibility categories (no-change, minor, behavioral, breaking). - Define header conventions (Deprecation-Date, Compat-Threshold, Suggested-Adapter). - Define telemetry signals (error delta, latency p95 delta, output-regression rate). Phase 2: Migration Assistant MVP (2 sprints) - CLI that takes customer config and target runtime version; runs a dry-run via saved prompts and model traces; outputs a compatibility report and suggested adapters. - Backend service to run longer compatibility suites for enterprise customers. Phase 3: Runtime integration (1 sprint) - Runtime emits compatibility headers and deprecation warnings, exposes /compatibility endpoint for automated checks. Phase 4: Rollout automation (1 sprint) - Canary policy that reads telemetry and blocks staged upgrades when thresholds exceeded. Each phase includes unit tests, integration harness, and documentation updates.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: run Migration Assistant against dogfood deployments and internal tenants. 2) Controlled beta: invite 5 external customers (opt-in) to use the CLI and give feedback; run backend full-suite for two customers. 3) Gradual enable: enable compatibility headers by default in edge nodes (no forced upgrades) and surface warning banners in Console. 4) Auto-upgrade rollout: after 4 weeks of stable telemetry and no critical regressions, enable automated suggestions and 10% opt-in auto-upgrades, increasing to 50% over two weeks. Canary gates: block if p95 latency increases >15% or output-regression rate >0.5% for critical prompt set. Rollback triggers: immediate rollback if error-rate increases by >2x baseline and customer impact is high.
compatibility_matrix: Compatibility categories: - Safe patch (x.y.z): backward-compatible bug fixes. No action needed. - Minor compatible (x.y+1): new features, opt-in flags, non-breaking defaults may change. Migration Assistant marks 'low risk' and suggests config adjustments. - Behavioral change (x+1.y): changes that may alter runtime scheduling, KV cache semantics, or streaming framing; requires validation run and optional adapter. - Breaking change (major bump): incompatible API or semantic shifts; requires explicit migration steps and a deprecation window. Fields to track per-change: affected endpoints, client-impact score, suggested adapter snippet, risk band, tests to run.
migration_guidance: - Use Migration Assistant dry-run before upgrading production. - Pin critical routes to a compatibility-safe model variant during migration. - For KV cache changes: run trace collection, compare KV-hit rates and apply cache-warming adapters suggested by assistant. - For API deprecations: Inspect Deprecation-* headers and follow suggested adapter code in the report. - For latency-sensitive workloads: perform canary at 1% then 5% using identical traffic shaping and collect p50/p95/p99 and tail-loss metrics. - Keep old runtime available for at least one deprecation window (default 60 days) and maintain automatic fallback routing during rollout.
test_plan: - Unit tests for compatibility report generator and adapter suggestion engine. - Integration test suite that runs representative prompt sets against old and new runtime versions and computes regression metrics. - Fuzz tests around streaming boundary conditions and KV cache eviction. - Load tests to validate canary gating thresholds. - Synthetic user journeys for the Console UI to confirm banners and migration steps are visible and actionable.
rollback_plan: - Automated: Canary gating will pause or rollback upgrades when thresholds are breached; orchestration will route traffic back to previous runtime variant. - Manual: Provide playbook steps in Console to: 1) pin traffic to previous runtime; 2) create incident ticket template; 3) run the migration-assistant diff to identify likely causes; 4) trigger hotfix patch if feasible, otherwise extend deprecation window and notify customers. - Post-rollback: collect traces and create postmortem with clear remediation tasks and versioning adjustments.
docs_and_comm: - Internal: Confluence page for policy and implementation notes, release checklist, and runbook. - External: Console docs article 'Using the Migration Assistant', migration checklist, and changelog entries per runtime release. - Customer comms: email template for breaking changes, deprecation scheduling, FAQ, and support playbook for enterprise customers. - Training: short webinar for Solutions Engineers and AE team covering migration flows.
notes: This ticket focuses on runtime-side compatibility signals and the Migration Assistant; SDK-specific adapter changes will be tracked in follow-ups. We will coordinate with Console and Solutions Engineering for customer beta selection.
